newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Seven die as cliff falls on Australian school group.
newsitem.headline: Seven die as cliff falls on Australian school group.

text.p: Seven people, some of them thought to be children, died on Friday when a cliff collapsed on a school group on a beach in Western Australia, police said.
It was not clear if others in the group were still trapped by the rockfall or had been rescued. Media reports said there were around 15 people in the group.
A police spokesman in nearby Margaret River told Reuters the the group were believed to have just finished a surfing lesson when the cliff face collapsed on them.
A woman from nearby Gracetown said the children had been watching a surfing competition on Friday afternoon. The Indian Ocean coastal area is popular with surfers.
"It was about three o'clock (0700 GMT) and the group was sitting under the cliff face watching the competition," said the woman, who did not want to be named.
"The cliff face was limestone and it just fell in. There are lots of ambulances around here and people are still working at the site," she said.
Acting police superintendent Bill Rowtcliff told Australian Broadcasting Corp television he did not know whether others in the group were still trapped in the rocks or had been rescued.
"Unfortunately, we have seven deceased people. I don't know if they were children, or adults who were with them, or some of each," Rowtcliff said.

"I've just seen a bunch of young people and they are obviously traumatised, but I can't see any physical injury on them," he added. The children in the group were believed to be aged 11 to 13, Rowtcliff said.
The accident happened at about three p.m. (0700 GMT) near the Cowaramup National Park about 200 km (120 miles) southwest of the Western Australia capital of Perth.
